newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares extend losses for sixth session.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares extend losses for sixth session.

text.p: Slovenian shares extended their losing streak to a sixth day on Thursday with the market weighed down by a more than seven percent fall in Probanka.
"There is no sign of fresh capital inflow to our market, and as I don't expect the political situation here to improve soon, the downward trend could continue for a while," one broker said.
The SBI index fell 16.91 points or 1.31 percent to 1,271.86, taking its losses to 2.86 percent this week.
Overall 11 shares fell, two rose and two were flat, while 13 were untraded. Turnover rose to 76.4 million tolars from 64.4 million.

"Custodian accounts, low liquidity and delayed ratification of the EU treaty are main factors hampering our market's activity. On top of that people's mistrust of the market is still high," one trader said.
In February the central bank blocked foreign investment, ordering international investors to open custody accounts to be able to trade in Slovenian securities.
Since then the blue-chip index has dropped over 23 percent, while average daily volume has shrunk to a fifth of its previous size.
Traders said ratification of the EU association treaty, which was signed a year ago, shoul attract some foreigners to resume trading in Slovenia.
Food maker Kolinska was the most active share, easing 0.75 percent to 1,851 tolars on volume of 10,282 shares for total turnover 19.1 million tolars.

Bank Probanka led the day's decliners, tumbling 7.62 percent to 19,400 tolars on volume of 490 shares. Traders said the bank fell due to its poor liquidity and that even a small sell-off can cause a huge fall in the share price.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, firming 0.77 percent to 7,900 tolars on volume of 171 shares.
Issue A of drug maker Lek remained flat at 24,200 tolars on volume of 770 shares for total turnover of 18.5 million tolars.
Lek was among the most active shares as it went ex-dividend today. Traders said the share has room down to between 23,000 and 23,500 tolars.

Shopping centre operator BTC, whose global depository receipts (GDRs) are expected to be listed on the SEAQ segment of the London Stock Exchange on June 20, firmed 0.69 percent to 14,500 tolars on volume of 231 shares.
